name: Good Subarrays
description: You are given an array $$$a_1, a_2, \dots , a_n$$$ consisting of integers from $$$0$$$ to $$$9$$$. A subarray $$$a_l, a_{l+1}, a_{l+2}, \dots , a_{r-1}, a_r$$$ is good if the sum of elements of this subarray is equal to the length of this subarray ($$$\sum\limits_{i=l}^{r} a_i = r - l + 1$$$). For example, if $$$a = [1, 2, 0]$$$, then there are $$$3$$$ good subarrays: $$$a_{1 \dots 1} = [1], a_{2 \dots 3} = [2, 0]$$$ and $$$a_{1 \dots 3} = [1, 2, 0]$$$. Calculate the number of good subarrays of the array $$$a$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 1000$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$) — the length of the array $$$a$$$. The second line of each test case contains a string consisting of $$$n$$$ decimal digits, where the $$$i$$$-th digit is equal to the value of $$$a_i$$$. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case print one integer — the number of good subarrays of the array $$$a$$$.
approach_summary: Express count as f(R) - f(L-1). Define memoized state dp[pos][tight][leading_zeros][cond] scanning digits from most to least significant in O(digits × base × states).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1398C — Good Subarrays [439. Digit DP]
topic_editorial.summary: Digit DP counting values in range $[L, R]$.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Counting valid integers in range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into $f(R) - f(L-1)$, where $f(X)$ counts valid integers in $[0, X]$. Numbers $\le X$ can be formed digit-by-digit from the most significant position. The constraint that the prefix does not exceed $X$ is tracked by a single boolean flag `tight`.
